verdict.rationale: mise keeps its data in plain-text, version-controlled files rather than a proprietary store, so there is nothing locked in to export. Configuration lives in TOML (`mise.toml`), env vars in `.env` files, and tasks can be standalone bash scripts. It also reads asdf `.tool-versions` and idiomatic files like `.node-version` as-is, which makes leaving for another version manager straightforward. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of migrating away or exporting state such as installed tools and trust settings, and independent hands-on reports of users leaving mise.
